definitions.explanation: A large volume or amount of something. Can function as a noun or as a na-adjective modifier.

examples.japanese: {多量|たりょう}の{水|みず}を{飲|の}む。
examples.english: To drink a large amount of water.

examples.japanese: アルコールを{多量|たりょう}に{摂取|せっしゅ}すると{危険|きけん}だ。
examples.english: Consuming alcohol in large quantities is dangerous.

examples.japanese: この{薬|くすり}を{多量|たりょう}に{服用|ふくよう}すると{副作用|ふくさよう}が{出|で}る{恐|おそ}れがある。
examples.english: Taking this medicine in large doses may cause side effects.

notes:
{多量|たりょう} combines {多|た} (many, much) and {量|りょう} (quantity, amount).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多量|たりょう}の + noun (a large amount of...)
- {多量|たりょう}に{摂取|せっしゅ}する (to consume in large quantities)
- {多量|たりょう}に{含|ふく}む (to contain in large amounts)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {多量|たりょう} vs. {大量|たいりょう}: Both mean "large quantity," but {大量|たいりょう} is more common in everyday usage and implies a greater scale. {多量|たりょう} tends to appear in technical, medical, or scientific contexts.
- {少量|しょうりょう} is the antonym (small quantity).
